record-red-deep.note: Hover on primary buttons; small red text, links, numerals.

record-red-soft.note: Tinted fills behind upsells and nudges; focus halos on drop zones.

record-red-line.note: Hairline on a tinted fill, link underlines, the HUD dot halo.

record-red-wash.note: Selected chips and the Shoot Cards column header.

marshmallow.note: The page ground; cool and neutral, never cream. The bloom on it is white light.

surface.note: Solid white: dialogs, menus, peek preview, focused inputs, glass base.

well.note: The paler inset a glass panel holds.

glass-edge.note: White hairline around every glass panel and pane.

ink.note: Structure: headings, the black nav pill, the 'Pay once' badge (white text), the closing card.

muted.note: Captions, meta and the grid lines (5.2:1 on Marshmallow).

camera-black.note: Bezels and camera bodies; the camera keeps its own world.

narrative.overview:
The page is one frosted pane on a marshmallow-white ground, lit from its lower left by a soft white light; the real camera is the subject the HUD points at. Every panel is the same material: a white glass gradient with a bright top edge and a cool shadow, holding paler wells for inputs and lists the way a dashboard card holds its chart. Bevelled corners, diagonal hatch marks and ringed HUD nodes give the glass an instrument's precision, so it reads as equipment rather than candy.

Density is moderate and editorial: generous section spacing, short copy, one clear action per block. Instrument Serif speaks in headlines; Inter instructs in everything you read in detail or press. Record Red is the only action colour. The light is white: it lives in the bloom and in a handful of small marks, never on a button.

The camera keeps its own world inside this one. Camera bodies, bezels and the cards drawn on their screens stay camera black and keep the card's own colours; the glass frames them, it never tints them.
keyCharacteristics: Marshmallow #F0F0F0 ground under a faint 40px line grid that rolls like calm water, with two soft blooms.
Frosted glass panels with white hairline edges, cool shadows and darker inner wells.
Three colours: Marshmallow white, Record Red and Ink black. Red for every action, selection and focus; white for the light (bloom, glass); black for structure (nav pill, badge, closing card, camera).
A white light rising from a corner of each large pane, answered by a faint red glow in the opposite corner.
Bevelled corners (`corner-shape: bevel`) on the hero frame, studio, panes, primary buttons and closing card.
Real camera bodies and real wedding photographs; cards always shown in a camera bezel.
Shape, not fade: things rise, unfold, iris open and blink; nothing crossfades.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Record Red marks the action, the selection and the focus; nothing else on the page is red-filled. The nav CTA is black precisely so it never competes with the studio's red button.

rules.name: The Three Colours Rule
rules.body: The palette is Marshmallow white (with white glass and white light), Record Red and Ink black. No other hue appears in site UI: no green, violet, blue, orange or pink. Light is white; colour means action.

rules.name: The Camera Keeps Its Colours Rule
rules.body: Cards rendered for the camera (pose cards with their red bars, the card-type tile SVGs, everything `assets/builder.js` draws) keep their own palette. That is product output, not site UI; the site palette never recolours it.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif for what we say, sans for what you do. Buttons, fields, labels and data are always Inter; headlines, numerals and the emphasised italic word are always Instrument Serif.

rules.name: The Heading Stands Alone Rule
rules.body: No kicker, eyebrow or tagline line above a heading. A section opens on its serif headline.

rules.name: The Glass Is The Material Rule
rules.body: Every panel (studio, pricing, FAQ, table, projects, dialogs, menus, the how-it-works strip) is the same glass: the white 90%→64% gradient, the white hairline edge, the Glass shadow. Inner content sits in Wells a step darker. Don't invent a second panel material.

rules.name: The Lift On Touch Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are calm at rest. Hover lifts a card 4px (a button 2px) and deepens its shadow; pressing snaps a button 1px down. With reduced motion, nothing moves; colour and border still change.

dos: Do show the real thing: real camera bodies, real cards in a camera bezel, photographs from real weddings.
Do build every panel from the one glass material, with Wells for the content it holds.
Do keep Record Red for the action, the selection and the focus, with the 2px Red focus ring on every control.
Do keep the palette to three colours: Marshmallow white, Record Red, Ink black; light is white.
Do use Instrument Serif for headlines and numerals, Inter for everything you read in detail or press.
Do lift cards 4px and buttons 2px on hover, with the matching shadow step.
Do give every tappable control a 44px hit area on touch screens.
donts: Don't put a kicker, eyebrow or tagline line above a heading.
Don't add a fourth colour (no green, violet, blue, orange or pink).
Don't recolour cards rendered for the camera to the site palette.
Don't warm the Marshmallow ground toward cream or tint shadows black; shadows stay cool navy.
Don't replace Inter or Instrument Serif; both are part of the shared NotaLucis identity.
Don't use stock imagery or invented testimonials, ratings or counts.
Don't show a card preview without its camera bezel.
Don't blur a dialog backdrop or use a blur() filter for the blooms; draw them as gradients.
